newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close marginally lower.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close marginally lower.

text.p: Selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and speculators offset purchases by mutual funds and pushed Delhi shares to a moderately lower close on the first day of settlement, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 1.18 points lower at 736.84.
Brokers said the closure of the Bombay Stock Exchange and most other regional exchanges for a Hindu holiday dried up buying support and kept a lid on prices.
"Domestic financial institutions buying was not sufficient to push up share prices," said Pradeep Malhotra of brokers Surge Investments.
"Investors and speculators have been withdrawing their investments from the capital market on fears of a further decline in share prices," said another broker who asked not to be identified.
Reliance Industries slipped 2.90 rupees to 194.10 on selling by FIIs as speculators booked profits, brokers said.
TISCO fell 2.75 rupees to 174.25 on speculative selling, they said.
State Bank of India quoted 4.10 rupees lower at 253.90, while ACC lost 26.05 rupees to 1,909.
Larsen and Toubro quoted 2.70 rupees lower at 238.25 and ITC lost 5.90 rupees to 280.10.
TELCO bucked the trend to gain 5 rupees at 450 on fund buying, brokers said.
